clue.text: For myself and for each member of the family, a friend

parts.note: per is Latin for 'for each', as in per head
a son is one member of a family
an ally is a friend who sides with you

explanation.surface: Someone sets aside something for themselves and for every relative and friend too.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in person, on one's own behalf, is doing it for oneself rather than through others.

clue.text: Sixty minutes needed to get university award

definitions.meaning: in angle measurement sixty minutes of arc make up one unit on the protractor
the qualification granted on completing a university course, such as a BA

explanation.surface: An hour of effort is what it takes to win a university prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sixty minutes' suggests an hour of time, but here the minutes are fractions of an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixty arc-minutes make one unit of angle, and the same word names an academic qualification.

clue.text: Bird in a duet struck a pose

indicators.note: in tells us the bird is set inside the reworked letters of the duet
struck suggests the letters of the duet are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: During a duet a bird suddenly struck a dramatic posture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struck' rearranges A DUET into ATUDE; the bird sits after its second letter. 'struck a pose' reads as one phrase, but 'struck' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike an attitude is to adopt a pose, a stance held for effect.

clue.text: The speed in G&S irritates

indicators.note: in places the speed inside the pair of initials

parts.note: G&S stands for Gilbert and Sullivan; here simply the letters G and S
rate is a word for speed, as in rate of knots

explanation.surface: The brisk tempo of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta annoys someone.
explanation.walkthrough: G&S is Gilbert and Sullivan, writers of Victorian comic operas; only their initials are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that grates on you jars on the nerves, so it irritates.

clue.text: Soft covering for body wrapped round a lover

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

indicators.note: wrapped round tells us the body covering encloses the a

parts.note: armour is protective covering for the body
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentle garment for the body is wrapped round a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is a lover, typically an illicit one in an affair.

clue.text: Sound performance, nothing missing

indicators.note: missing tells us the letter for nothing is taken out

parts.note: doing is a performance or carrying out of something
O, shaped like zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A sound performance comes off without a hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but it is the noun definition: a ringing noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A ding is the ringing noise a bell makes, so it is a sound.

clue.text: Lifejacket could make me sweat

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters of me sweat can be turned into something else

explanation.surface: Wearing a lifejacket in the heat would make me perspire.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mae West is RAF slang for an inflatable lifejacket, named after the buxom film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Wartime airmen named their inflatable life vest after the actress Mae West's famous figure.

clue.text: Ponderous maid's unusual way of doing things

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of the two words are arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: the possessive s gives no letter

explanation.surface: A slow-moving servant has an odd method of going about her work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for a method of operating means a characteristic way of working.

clue.text: A smiler could demonstrate a philosophical outlook

indicators.note: could demonstrate suggests the letters of a smiler can be shown in another form

explanation.surface: Someone who smiles might display a particular view of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is a philosophical position that the world exists independently of our minds.

clue.text: Lad is a monster — exceptional insensitivity

indicators.note: exceptional tells us the letters fall in an out-of-the-ordinary arrangement

explanation.surface: A boy is called a brute for his remarkable lack of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroitness is clumsiness, especially tactlessness in dealing with people, hence insensitivity.

clue.text: I'd had back injury before start of the seizure

indicators.note: before puts the injury ahead of the following letter
back tells us I'd is turned to read the other way

parts.note: I'd, without its apostrophe, gives the letters I and D
a strain is a muscle injury

indicators.note: start of takes the opening letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Someone who had hurt their back went on to suffer a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' is a link word; 'I'd' stands for 'I had'. 'seizure' suggests a fit, but here it means the legal taking of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraint is the legal seizure of someone's property to force payment of a debt.

clue.text: Very helpful person in a new set

parts.note: to gel is to set, as jelly does

explanation.surface: A really useful helper joins a fresh group.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a kind, obliging person an angel is an everyday figure of speech.

clue.text: Foreign money given to Home Counties faculty

parts.note: the sen is a small coin unit in Japan and elsewhere in Asia
the Home Counties around London lie in the south-east of England, SE

explanation.surface: Overseas cash is handed to the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense such as sight or hearing is one of the body's faculties.

clue.text: Without blemish, as a leopard isn't?

definitions.meaning: clean and unmarked, morally or physically
a leopard famously cannot change its spots, so it is never free of them

explanation.surface: Something is flawless, unlike the big cat with its famous markings.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half plays on the saying that a leopard cannot change its spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarked by any spot or stain, so pure and without blemish.

clue.text: The old man, character not right for the board

parts.note: pa is an informal word for one's father, the old man

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for right is dropped

parts.note: a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: Dad turns out to be a character not fit to sit on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests a committee, but it is the artist's thin board for mixing paints.
explanation.definitionFit: A palette is the thin board on which an artist mixes colours.

clue.text: You may catch the smell of an American in a Roosevelt

indicators.note: catch tells us the old word for you holds the smell within it

parts.note: thee is an archaic form of you
odor is the American spelling of the British odour, a smell

explanation.surface: You might pick up an American's scent on one of the Roosevelts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch the smell' suggests sniffing, but 'catch' is the container, and 'of an American' asks for the US spelling without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Roosevelt was the twenty-sixth US President, one of the famous Roosevelts.

clue.text: Storm has ripped apart a celebration

parts.note: torn means ripped apart
a do is an informal word for a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A party is wrecked by violent weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, a kind of storm.

clue.text: Valve gets most of the rubbish let out

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter of the is taken

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of let are put out of place

explanation.surface: A valve lets out most of the waste material.
explanation.definitionFit: A throttle is the valve controlling how much fuel or steam reaches an engine.

clue.text: Society's taken in by the merry, dissolute versifier

indicators.note: taken in by tells us the society letter sits inside the rearranged words
dissolute, meaning loose-living, suggests the letters of the merry break loose

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A club is welcomed by a jolly, debauched poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissolute' rearranges the eight letters into RHYMETER, and the society's letter goes in after RHYME.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a writer of verse, usually a modest or mediocre one.

clue.text: Car takes wrong route crossing river

indicators.note: crossing tells us the jumbled route straddles the river letter
wrong suggests the letters of route are put the wrong way

explanation.surface: A motorist goes the wrong way and drives over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes TOUER from ROUTE, and 'crossing' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourer is a car built for long-distance touring.

clue.text: A hundred remaining in the chasm

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
left means remaining, as in what is left over

explanation.surface: A hundred people are left stranded in the gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft is a split or fissure in rock, a narrow chasm.

clue.text: Make box for putting drug into

indicators.note: into tells us the drug goes inside the box

parts.note: a crate is a wooden packing box
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone builds a container for smuggling narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: To create is to make or bring something into being.

clue.text: Distinguished editor not coming to the fore

indicators.note: coming to the fore puts not in front of the editor

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An eminent editor fails to step forward into the limelight.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known and respected, so distinguished.

clue.text: Former leader of country, past it, obviously hides

indicators.note: hides tells us the answer is concealed within the run of words

explanation.surface: An ex-leader of a nation who is plainly over the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Marshal Tito led Yugoslavia, a country that no longer exists, from 1945 to 1980.
explanation.definitionFit: Tito was the long-serving leader of Yugoslavia, now a former state.

clue.text: Hate punt going wrong? Finally decide to bet even more

indicators.note: going wrong suggests the letters of hate punt go awry
Finally takes the closing letter of decide

explanation.surface: A gambler loathes a losing wager but in the end raises the stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' makes UPTHEANT from HATE PUNT; 'punt' is British slang for a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise the ante is to increase the stake in a bet, so bet even more.

clue.text: One after the other reported junior American doctor

indicators.note: reported signals that the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: in turn means one after the other

explanation.surface: Someone describes a young US medic as being reported in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: An interne, also spelt intern, is a junior hospital doctor in the United States.

clue.text: Liquid preparations from old books fed to animals

indicators.note: fed to tells us the old books go inside the animals

parts.note: lions are animals
OT is the Old Testament, the old books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Ointments are made from ancient volumes thrown to the beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed to animals' evokes Christians thrown to lions, fitting the Bible books.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotions are liquid preparations applied to the skin.
